citation: K. Zhong et al., Experimental study of PAM-4, CAP-16, and DMT for 100 Gb/s short reach optical transmission systems, Optics Express 23(2), 1176–1189 (2015)
method: Direct native raster extraction with PyMuPDF and labeled-grid calibration. The blue response has no vector path. PDF vector and bitmap annotations overlay the native plot, which retains the response under the 17 GHz dot and dash line.

frequency_mapping.paper_AWG_source: Section 2.3, printed page 1180, reports the 63 GSa/s DMT transmitter AWG
frequency_mapping.paper_measurement_source: Section 3, printed page 1182, describes the discrete AWG sweep, 80 GSa/s receiver scope and reported channel bandwidth of 17 GHz

vertical_axis.label: S21 (dB)
vertical_axis.definition: End-to-end channel transmission magnitude in dB. After subtracting the low-frequency reference, amplitude ratio is 10^(normalized_dB/20).

low_frequency_reference.assumption: Treat the first visible near-DC sample as the unity reference. Assume a flat normalized response between DC and this sample when modeling DC. The flat extension to DC belongs to the model. The CSV starts at the first visible plotted sample.

trace_reading.native_pixel_origin: Zero-based pixel-center coordinates from the top left
trace_reading.center: Median blue row in each native column, with both occupied row endpoints retained
trace_reading.read_error_basis: The blue-column half thickness plus a half-pixel axis allowance describes raster reading precision. The original measurement uncertainty is unspecified. The low-frequency reference adds its own reading error to normalized values.
